responsibility: Houses the main implementation of the RISC-V GCC backend. It owns core target logic for register and address legitimacy, symbol classification and address splitting, frame layout and prologue/epilogue generation, calling convention decisions, move expansion, small-data and section selection, target hooks, scheduling/tuning integration, vector-mode support queries, and the registration of all targetm hooks that connect the RISC-V port to GCC’s middle end and RTL back end.
same_name_distinction: Within the `riscv` same-name group, this `.cc` file is the main executable backend implementation: it defines the target logic and installs the `targetm` hooks that drive code generation. Unlike `riscv.h`'s macro/configuration interface, `riscv.md`'s RTL pattern descriptions, and `riscv.opt`'s option metadata, this file contains the procedural C++ backend behavior.
